C-TABLE-FIT-PERSISTENCE.IntentSummary: Repair the host fit-serialization gap the C-TABLE-FOOTER native review exposed: a failing unit first, then sanitizeEntry keeps muya's fit flag (Full width wins contradictions), the same-tick transition and the save→reopen persistence pinned in both engines, and the native same-frame confirmation handed to the fresh isolated artifact with the conditional three-point instrumentation rule.
C-TABLE-FIT-PERSISTENCE.ExecutionPolicy: Execute sequentially after the FIX-008 and FIX-011 bundles. Durable scope M-012/V-M-012 overlaps C-TABLE-FOOTER (which stays active pending its focused re-acceptance) and C-FIX-008-VIEWER-PAN-CUES; this bundle touches only the host store util, its tests and the table-layout spec.

MustContain.Text: a fit entry survives the save → load roundtrip (C-TABLE-FIT-PERSISTENCE)

Corner.Name: Correctness — the gap
Corner.Expected: The failing unit reproduces the owner-visible defect class on main (fit dropped by sanitizeEntry), then the repair keeps fit through sanitize, normalizeStore, storeWithFileEntries and both IO flows; Full width wins a contradictory entry exactly as muya's sanitizer rules.

Corner.Name: Correctness — schema extension honesty
Corner.Expected: The pre-existing exact-shape expectations gain the fit field rather than being loosened; entryFor carries fit; no old case is deleted.

Corner.Name: Correctness — transition
Corner.Expected: One click on the «Fit to page» toggle leaves ag-table-full-width and flips the label in the same tick (asserted synchronously after click(), no re-render wait).

Corner.Name: Correctness — persistence
Corner.Expected: The e2e proves the fit flag in the mt::prefs::set payload and, after reopen (open-new-tab dedup → UPDATE_CURRENT_FILE → the C-65 load hook), the wide table stays out of Full width with the label «Full width»; the stat mock is path-aware so the pruning keeps the document while the `.before` sidecar auto-diff does not fire.

Corner.Name: Correctness — native boundary
Corner.Expected: The native same-frame transition is NOT claimed fixed by the host repair; the evidence names the fresh-artifact confirmation as the remaining step, with the three-point instrumentation rule (toolbar action received → Muya layout emitted → host payload saved) if browser passes and native fails.

Corner.Name: Security and Privacy
Corner.Expected: Synthetic fixtures under /tmp/mark-e2e only; the prefs mock lives in the page; no secrets or owner data.

Corner.Name: UX
Corner.Expected: Accepted C-TABLE-FOOTER visuals are untouched; the focused owner recheck covers only Full width → Fit to page → reopen.

Corner.Name: Performance and Footprint
Corner.Expected: One extra boolean per stored entry; no IO or render-path change; suite budgets unchanged.

Corner.Name: Scope hygiene
Corner.Expected: Only the host util, its tests, the table-layout spec and projections; muya is untouched (its sanitizer already kept fit).

Corner.Name: Delivery discipline
Corner.Expected: Nothing is queued or accepted here; C-TABLE-FOOTER re-acceptance and admission wait for the focused native recheck on the fresh artifact.

T-001.Title: Failing unit, then the sanitizer repair

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The fit cases fail on the unmodified sanitizeEntry (verified before the fix), then sanitizeEntry keeps fit with the Full-width-wins rule; the pre-existing suite passes on the extended schema; the module contract bumps to v1.1.0.
The table-layout spec gains the C-TABLE-FIT-PERSISTENCE case: same-tick flip, fit flag in the prefs payload, reopen keeps Fit — green in chromium and webkit-tables with the rest of the spec.

Verification.Command: npm run build && npx playwright test tests/e2e/table-layout.spec.ts --project=chromium --project=webkit-tables

T-003.Title: Projections, evidence and the native handoff

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: V-M-012 scenario-72 recorded; M-012 graph summary line added; evidence.json names the native confirmation and the conditional instrumentation rule; grace lint --assertions current zero errors; the repair joins the fresh isolated Mark Test for the owner's Fit-only recheck.

Review.Findings: Correctness and Contracts: the defect chain was re-derived from the C-TABLE-FOOTER evidence diagnosticBoundary (host sanitizer gap proven; native same-frame unproven) — the plan keeps those two claims separate rather than letting the host fix imply the native one. FINDING (fixed): the first draft asserted the pre-state markers as active baselines; replaced with existence pins plus the git-history pointer (the FIX-008/FIX-011 lesson). Security and Privacy: clean. UX and Docs: the Fit-only recheck boundary is explicit. Performance and Footprint: one boolean per entry. CornerMatrix (10 corners) added before approval.
None. The targets pin the exact sanitizer line, both test surfaces and the V-M-012 scenario; every criterion maps to a task and a command; the muya non-goal and the native boundary are unambiguous.

Executor walk surfaced two harness facts now baked into the corners: the table-layout spec boots untitled documents (a named file must be opened over the empty boot tab for the persistence path) and the shim's default mt_fs_stat reports "not a file", which would prune the persisted entry — the path-aware stat mock also prevents the `.before`-sidecar auto-diff from hijacking the editor.

Four independent passes over the executed change. Correctness and Contracts: the failing-first sequence was honored (2 tests red on main, green after); the schema extension updated every exact-shape expectation; the e2e proves both halves in both engines (16 passed). FINDING (fixed): a first-draft reopen via CLOSE_TAB landed on the welcome screen (opening a file had replaced the empty boot tab) — the reopen now rides the open-new-tab dedup path (UPDATE_CURRENT_FILE → the C-65 load hook), which is also the closer analogue of the owner's scenario. Security and Privacy: clean. UX and Docs: contracts bumped (v1.1.0 / spec v1.7.0); scenario-72 and the M-012 summary line recorded. Performance and Footprint: clean. The native same-frame confirmation on the fresh artifact remains the named next step.
